title: BACE: Biochemistry & Molecular Biology - Biochemistry & Molecular Biology - DNA Replication
subject: Biochemistry & Molecular Biology

questions.q: During DNA replication, which enzyme is responsible for unwinding the DNA double helix at the replication fork?
questions.explain: DNA Helicase is the enzyme responsible for breaking the hydrogen bonds between base pairs, thereby unwinding the DNA double helix to create the replication fork.
questions.subject: Biochemistry & Molecular Biology

questions.q: Why are Okazaki fragments formed during DNA replication?
options: Because DNA Polymerase can only synthesize DNA in the $3' \rightarrow 5'$ direction
Because DNA Polymerase can only synthesize DNA in the $5' \rightarrow 3'$ direction and the strands are antiparallel
Because the leading strand requires multiple primers
Because helicase opens the DNA in discontinuous segments
questions.explain: DNA strands are antiparallel, and DNA Polymerase can only synthesize in the $5' \rightarrow 3'$ direction. Therefore, on the lagging strand ($3' \rightarrow 5'$ template), synthesis must occur discontinuously away from the replication fork, creating Okazaki fragments.
questions.subject: Biochemistry & Molecular Biology

questions.q: What is the primary role of DNA Ligase in DNA replication?
options: To join the phosphodiester backbone of Okazaki fragments
questions.explain: DNA Ligase catalyzes the formation of a phosphodiester bond between the $3'$-OH end of one DNA fragment and the $5'$-phosphate end of another, effectively sealing nicks in the backbone, such as those between Okazaki fragments.
questions.subject: Biochemistry & Molecular Biology

questions.q: The proofreading activity of DNA Polymerase involves which enzymatic capability?
questions.explain: DNA Polymerases proofread by using their $3' \rightarrow 5'$ exonuclease activity to remove an incorrectly added nucleotide at the $3'$ end before resuming synthesis.
questions.subject: Biochemistry & Molecular Biology

questions.q: Which of the following proteins prevents the single-stranded DNA from re-annealing or forming secondary structures during replication?
questions.explain: Single-Strand Binding (SSB) proteins bind to the separated DNA strands near the replication fork to prevent them from re-annealing or forming hairpins, keeping the template accessible for the polymerase.
questions.subject: Biochemistry & Molecular Biology

questions.q: Topoisomerase (or DNA Gyrase in bacteria) helps in DNA replication by:
options: Relieving the torsional strain (supercoiling) ahead of the replication fork
questions.explain: As Helicase unwinds the DNA, positive supercoils build up ahead of the fork. Topoisomerase relieves this torsional strain by cutting and rejoining DNA strands to relax the supercoiling.
